text: 7.6 In today's show we'll be interviewing the talented fashion designer Aisha Al-Husseini. Hot on the heels of her Fashion Week show, Aisha's new collection is very popular in Doha. She got the attention of the fashion world with her unique designs, which combine traditional Muslim fashion with French chic. Aisha, thank you for coming to the studio. Thank you for having me. First of all, can you tell me where you get your ideas from? Well, I come from a Muslim family. My parents are both from Qatar. I was born there, but then we traveled a lot. I went to school in New York and I went to a design school there. These days, I spend my time traveling between Qatar and the United States. How did you feel about growing up in New York? Well, as a teenager in New York, I had a lot of problems trying to dress in a modest way. For example, when you look at summer fashion in New York, the trend is always to wear skirts, shorts and sleeveless shirts. I didn't feel comfortable wearing them, but at the same time, my friends thought it was strange to wear long sleeves and jeans in the summer. So I've always tried to combine my culture with fashion. As a teenager, I would make my own clothes like colorful skirts and scarves. I wanted my designs to be individual. They were unique and eventually, people admired my clothes rather than laughed at me. I see. So do you know what ideas most people have about Muslim clothes? Well, I think there's a lot of misunderstanding about Muslim clothes. The thing is that when you say Muslim fashion, people in New York think of a burqa, you know, like the blue or black cloaks which cover women from head to toe. And could you explain what you think Muslim fashion is? Let me give you an example. When I first started at design school, my teachers would ask me strange questions such as how I was going to stay in the fashion business if I'm not going to design miniskirts or sleeveless shirts. But as far as I'm concerned, there is much more to fashion than showing your body. There are millions of Muslim women who live in the United States and Europe who want to wear fashionable clothes. There are also women who simply like to dress in a modest way. So are you saying that there is a need for fashionable clothes for Muslim women? Absolutely. We want to be fashionable and be ourselves at the same time. My feeling is this. I want to create clothes which are modest but at the same time give women confidence, clothes which allow women to be themselves. I see what you mean. So how would you describe your style? Well, many reviewers have described my style as traditional chic. And I guess I'd agree with them. What I think is that combining traditional with chic is a huge area in fashion. I keep my eye on the fashion trends in other countries. When you look at the works of other designers in China and India, you can see that many traditional styles are being reused by young designers. Above all, people like to be individuals and show their cultural roots. They like to show where they come from. As I understand it, your designs are must haves for Muslim women outside the United States as well. Could you tell me more about that? Yes. In addition to New York and Paris, I sell my collection in big cities like Doha, Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Another thing is that I also receive requests for my clothes from women in Pakistan, Indonesia, Singapore and Malaysia. So someday I might open stores there. Well, I hope you decide to go for it. That would make a lot of women around the world very happy. So Aisha, thank you for coming to the studio today. It was my pleasure. Anytime. Thank you.
